claims.statement: The release-please manifest has nine independently released package baselines—Deep Agents 0.7.32, ACP 0.0.13, Code 0.2.2, Talon 0.1.0, Daytona 0.0.9, Modal 0.0.7, Runloop 0.0.7, Vercel 0.0.2, and QuickJS 0.3.11—and configuration creates separate draft Python release PRs with pre-1.0 bump behavior while delegating publication to release.yml.

The lockfile refresh helper computes changed manifest owners plus their reverse transitive local-source consumers and runs `uv lock` with each package’s selected Python version; the ordinary checker instead checks directly touched packages, or every discovered package when invoked without paths, and reports a concrete repair command for an out-of-date lock.

Release-note curation executes trusted automation checked out from `main` and treats release-PR content as untrusted API data: it never checks out or executes that content, confines model drafting to a fixed request without filesystem, shell, or network tools, and reserves mutations for helpers using a short-lived GitHub App token.

The release-note helper accepts a release PR only when it is open, internal to the base repository, targets `main`, uses the configured release-branch prefix, and has a title whose component agrees with that branch; it derives the changelog path from the Release Please configuration registry rather than trusting PR-derived paths.
Curated-note commands require a ready release PR and write-level maintainer permission, reject ambiguous multiple commands, and serialize runs per PR without cancelling an in-flight operation.

Draft and apply fail closed against stale or forged curation state: drafts fingerprint generated entries and reject model metadata or version-heading injection; apply requires a valid bot-owned draft, detects relevant package changes since drafting, preserves the generated heading, and rejects new generated entries.

Merging a release PR triggers publication only after release-please identifies a release-form commit and package changelog change, while the workflow blocks empty commits because pathless commits would otherwise fan out to every component.

The release process preserves one-version-one-artifact integrity: a manual recovery release selects an exact source SHA whose package metadata declares the requested version, and after PyPI publication operators must not republish the version or move its tag.

The targeted lock checker resolves ACP, Code, Evals, and Talon with Python 3.14 and all other discovered packages with 3.12, whereas the aggregate `libs/Makefile` maps only ACP to 3.14; targeted refresh commands therefore preserve the checker’s package-specific lock policy.

Code's local `make check` treats an SDK pin older than the workspace SDK as advisory but distinguishes it from malformed or unsupported version data, which exits as an indeterminate error; the release workflow is the hard gate that rejects an older Code SDK pin unless its dangerous bypass is selected.

After Deep Agents is published, the SDK-pin automation creates or updates one Code `chore(deps):` pull request when Code is behind, regenerates its lockfile, and leaves an ahead-of-workspace pin unchanged for intentional prerelease coordination.

The shared CI uv setup pins uv to 0.13.6, accepts a requested Python major.minor version, enables a pruned dependency cache by default, and scopes its cache inputs to package manifests, locks, and requirements files.

Lockfile discovery includes library packages with Makefiles, partner packages, and every example directory with a `pyproject.toml`; eval and example locks remain package-local artifacts with their own Python and platform resolution metadata.

The release-please scope guard runs its detector and configuration from the trusted PR base revision, fails closed if GitHub’s changed-file list is incomplete, and requires an explicit `ci:allow-lockfile-release` label to acknowledge detected bump-worthy lockfile-only or multi-component fan-out.

Release Please serializes release-branch mutation only after repository-wide pending publication state is clear: unreadable state blocks maintenance, a pending publish can defer refresh, and the workflow waits across all pending packages because recomputation covers all components.

The package release build validates a non-dangerous release SHA is reachable from main and that its `pyproject.toml` version matches the requested version, then aborts before publication if that package version already exists on PyPI.
